title: Modelling across a Reactions unit

moments.what: Think aloud while balancing two equations, including one where you get stuck (half an O<sub>2</sub>) and recover.
moments.why: Students hear the decisions — where to start, why oxygen last — and see that getting stuck is a normal part of the work.

moments.what: Pairs balance equations, one thinking aloud, with a prompt card: Where do I start? Why? Does it check?
moments.why: Coaching: students rehearse the moves while you listen for which ones are missing.

moments.what: Model again on a new kind of problem — predicting the products of a precipitation reaction — then hand straight over to pairs.
moments.why: Shows that narrating decisions works on unfamiliar content, not just on balancing.

moments.what: Remove the prompt card. Students write one margin note per problem about a decision they made.
moments.why: The questions move from the card into students’ heads.

moments.what: Set an unfamiliar reaction type with no prompts. Listen to pairs and collect worked solutions: who checks, unprompted?
moments.why: Tells you whether the habit is independent, and which students need more coaching.

summary: Model early with a real stuck point, coach with a prompt card, model once more on new content, fade the card, then check for unprompted use on an unfamiliar problem.
